table_data.paper_title: Dynamical Origins and Equation-of-State Constraints from the Eccentric Millisecond Pulsar PSR J1903+0327

columns.Pulsar Classification & System Type: Eccentric Millisecond Pulsar (MSP) in a 95-day orbit
columns.Primary Mass Measurement Methodology: Post-Keplerian parameters: Shapiro delay, apsidal motion, proper motion; Optical spectroscopy for radial velocities
columns.Equation of State Constraints: Rules out soft equations of state containing hyperons, bosons, or free quarks at nuclear saturation densities

table_data.paper_title: Record-Breaking Mass Measurement of the Fastest Spinning Pulsar PSR J0952−0607

columns.Pulsar Classification & System Type: Black Widow MSP (fastest spinning disk pulsar)
columns.Primary Mass Measurement Methodology: Multicolor light curve modeling and companion radial velocities; Direct-heating model fitting
columns.Companion Object Nature: Very faint, low-mass companion within Roche lobe (heated by pulsar irradiation)
columns.Equation of State Constraints: Establishes minimum maximum mass M_max > 2.19 M_sun (1 sigma), implying stiff equation of state

table_data.paper_title: Inclination Angle Decay and Its Critical Role in Pulsar Braking Torque and Galactic Population Synthesis

columns.Primary Spin-Down Mechanism: Vacuum dipole radiation with variable inclination
columns.Treatment of Inclination Angle (Alpha): Negative decay rate ($\dot{\alpha} < 0$); critical role in torque
columns.Braking Index Behavior: Implicitly variable due to alpha evolution; not fixed n=3
columns.Population Synthesis Focus: Reproducing P-Pdot diagram without long birth periods or B-field decay

table_data.paper_title: Particle Wind Dynamics and Pulsar Death Boundaries in Rotational Evolution Models

columns.Treatment of Inclination Angle (Alpha): Calculated parameter; evolves from dipole-dominated to wind-dominated
columns.Braking Index Behavior: Variable; lower between glitches due to higher particle density
columns.Population Synthesis Focus: Individual source evolution (Crab) and death valley trajectories
columns.Key Physical Constraints/Findings: Particle density ~10^3 x Goldreich-Julian; Evolution towards death valley, not magnetars

table_data.paper_title: Population Synthesis of Isolated Pulsars: Comparing Magnetic Dipole and Hybrid Torque Models

columns.Primary Spin-Down Mechanism: Standard Magnetic Dipole vs. Hybrid (Contopoulos & Spitkovsky)
columns.Treatment of Inclination Angle (Alpha): Random alignment angles; torque should not depend strongly on inclination
columns.Braking Index Behavior: Analyzed as a key property affecting population distribution
columns.Population Synthesis Focus: Comparing models to reproduce observable P-Pdot diagram characteristics
columns.Key Physical Constraints/Findings: Magnetic dipole model fits better than hybrid; Period-dependent luminosity essential

table_data.paper_title: Extreme Glitch Activity and Negative Braking Index in Young X-ray Pulsar J0537−6910

columns.Primary Glitch Phenomenon: Extreme activity (~3.5/yr); large spin-ups every ~100 d; 45 total glitches over 13 yr
columns.Correlation Evidence: Strong correlation between glitch spin-up size and time to next glitch (unique among pulsars)
columns.Theoretical Model Framework: Multicomponent model accounting for crust and core neutron superfluid dynamics
columns.Braking Index Characteristics: Negative long-term braking index (n_l = -1.22(4)); spin-down rate increased over 13 yr
columns.Moment of Inertia Constraints: Limits placed on fractional moment of inertia of spin-up component and sustained velocity difference

table_data.paper_title: Intra-Binary Shock Heating Model Reproduces Asymmetric Light Curves in Evaporating Binary PSR J2215+5135

columns.Companion Roche Lobe Status: Roche lobe filling (implied by context of other papers in cluster, though this paper focuses on light curve asymmetry)
columns.Key Observational Evidence: Asymmetric optical light curves of PSR J2215+5135 fitted with IBS model

table_data.paper_title: Universal Irradiation Efficiencies and Roche Lobe Underfilling in Energetic Fermi Millisecond Pulsar Companions

columns.Primary Physical Mechanism for Orbital E: Thermal contraction or incomplete ablation; challenges standard Roche-lobe overflow necessity
columns.Irradiation Efficiency and Heating Model: Universal efficiency of 10%–30% reprocessed into heat; direct pulsar illumination vs. alternative mechanisms
columns.Companion Roche Lobe Status: Significant underfilling observed in J0023+0923 and J2256-1024 despite radio eclipses
columns.Key Observational Evidence: Optical light curve synthesis using Gemini/NTT data showing universal irradiation range
